chapters.title: Why it really ended (your side of it)
chapters.teaser: Not who was right. What your soul was doing while it fell apart.

chapters.title: Your breakup pattern
chapters.teaser: How you end things, how you grieve, and the habit that slows you down.

chapters.title: Why you keep checking
chapters.teaser: What the pull back toward them is really asking for.

chapters.title: So, will they come back? The honest answer
chapters.teaser: What a chart can and can't tell you, and the question that matters more.

chapters.title: If they ever reach out
chapters.teaser: Three questions to ask before you reply, built for your soul.

chapters.title: What you do now
chapters.teaser: The next small steps that help, whatever they decide.

text.why-it-ended: Gyeong Metal is the blade: direct, loyal, decisive. You say what you mean and expect the same in return. In your last relationship that honesty was a gift, and sometimes a weapon. Under stress you can end a conversation with one sentence that's true and still lands far too hard. Or you decided early what was right and stopped negotiating. Metal souls also tend to end things cleanly once trust breaks. If this ended fast, a line was probably crossed, or you felt one coming. Either way, be honest with yourself about whether you left room for the softer conversation.
text.your-breakup-pattern: Your breakups are clean cuts. Once Gyeong Metal decides, it's decided, and you don't do the on-and-off thing. You delete, archive, move on. It looks strong, and often it is. But sometimes the speed is a way of not feeling the wound. Metal souls grieve in sudden waves: fine for weeks, then flattened by a song in the supermarket. That's not going backwards. That's the feeling catching up with you. The pattern to watch is mistaking toughness for healing. You can be strong and sad on the very same day, and nobody will think less of you.
text.the-pull: What pulls you back is usually loyalty, or a question of fairness. Was it handled right? Did they understand what really happened? Gyeong Metal hates loose ends and unfair outcomes. You might also miss the person who could handle your directness without crumbling, which is rarer than people think. That's worth admitting. But notice that you can respect someone and still be right to leave. Respect doesn't require reunion. Write down what you'd say in one last honest conversation. You may find the real need is clarity, not the person.
text.the-honest-answer: Their choices can't be read from your chart, and we won't pretend otherwise. What we can see is the blade. Gyeong Metal values loyalty above almost everything, so if trust was broken, getting back together would need real repair, not an apology text. If you were the one who cut hard, ask whether you'd return with more patience and fewer verdicts. Either way, a second try with a Metal soul only works if both people can talk straight without trying to win. That's the honest bar. If it can't be reached, the clean ending was the right one.
text.if-they-reach-out: If they reach out, you'll want to give a direct answer immediately. That's fine, as long as it's the answer you'd still give tomorrow. Ask yourself: has the reason we ended actually changed? If trust was the problem, what would rebuilding it look like, specifically, week by week? Gyeong Metal does well with clear terms. If you're open to talking, say so, along with what you need to hear. If you're not, say that kindly and briefly. Skip the dramatic final speech. You already won the argument. Now you only have to choose.
text.what-you-do-now: Sharpen something else. Gyeong Metal heals through challenge, so pick one: a fitness goal, a difficult skill, a big work project you've been putting off. But also do the soft thing you'd normally skip. Let a friend sit with you while you're low. Say that hurt out loud. Metal is forged in fire and cooled in water, so give yourself both, effort and rest, in roughly equal measure. You don't need to be bulletproof this month. You only need to be honest with yourself, which has always been your best quality anyway.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You were honest and loyal, Gyeong. Those are rare.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And sometimes you used honesty like a sword. At dinner.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Grief can show up weeks later. That's normal.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Crying at a supermarket song doesn't cancel your strength.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: If they reach out, say clearly what you need.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: No final speeches. You already won. Now just choose.

spring.intro: A spring axe has a whole forest in front of it. Wood ruled your birth season, Gyeong, and Metal cuts Wood, so you were born facing a lot to handle, with the strength to handle it. In love you probably took charge: decided, fixed, protected. You show care by acting. The breakup might feel like a job left half-done, and that bothers you more than you admit. You may be planning conversations, rehearsing the clean version of the ending. The spring blind spot is effort spread thin, swinging at too many trees at once. Pick one task: your own sleep, your own week. You can't chop your way back into someone's heart, and you shouldn't have to.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Rehearsing the perfect closing speech in the shower again? Thought so.

summer.intro: Metal born in summer goes through the forge. Fire ruled your birth season, Gyeong, and Fire melts Metal, so you grew up under heat and pressure and came out tempered. You're tough, loyal and allergic to drama. In the relationship you probably took a lot before reacting, then reacted all at once. Clean cut. Done. But summer metal stays warm long after it leaves the fire. You might act finished while still running hot underneath, and that's where the checking comes from. Your pride says don't look back. Your heart keeps looking. Neither is wrong. Let the cooling happen slowly instead of plunging it into cold water and pretending it never glowed.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Still warm after the forge is normal. It means it mattered to you.

autumn.intro: Born in autumn, Gyeong, you're metal at full strength. Metal ruled the season and doubled your element, so you're decisive, principled and very hard to bend. In breakups that usually means one of two things: you ended it sharply, or you refused to let it end until you'd won the point. Either way, the blade was out. Strong autumn metal can confuse being right with being close. You may have been right about plenty. The question worth asking is what being right cost. If you keep checking on them, it might be to confirm your verdict rather than because you miss them. Put the sword down for a week. See what you feel without it in your hand.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You were right. Congratulations. Was being right warm at night?

winter.intro: Winter Gyeong is cold steel beside a dark river. Water ruled your season, and Metal generates Water, so your toughness flows out as thought, strategy and quiet feeling. You look composed. Inside, you're running analysis on every exchange from the last three months. In love you probably showed care through loyalty and action, and kept the softer feelings in reserve. After the breakup that reserve is leaking out as late-night thinking. It's not weakness. It's metal finally letting water through. The pull back is often the conversation you never had, the one where you said the soft thing. You can still say it, to a journal, a friend, yourself. It doesn't have to be to them.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Write the soft thing down, Gyeong. It deserves to exist somewhere.

strength.strong: Your chart reinforces your metal, Gyeong, so you're tough, decisive and fond of clean lines. In love you protect fiercely and say things straight. In a breakup that strength can cut too deep: words that were true and still too sharp, or an ending delivered like a verdict. You might also be holding your ground in your head, refusing to soften even privately. The blind spot is that strength without softness feels like armour to someone else. If you're replaying it, find one moment you could have been gentler. That's not losing. That's a sharper edge for next time.
strength.weak: Your metal doesn't get much backup in your chart, Gyeong, so you've built toughness on top of a softer core. In love you probably acted strong while giving in quietly: their plans, their mood, their version. You might have swallowed things until you snapped, or never snapped at all. After the breakup you may feel brittle, tough outside and shaky inside. Let someone see the inside. Strength is being able to say this hurt me, plainly. Before thinking about them, rebuild your edge with routines, rest and people who respect your no.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood means you push for growth and answers, even in heartbreak. You want a plan for getting over it, maybe even a plan for getting them back. Slow down. Not everything grows on schedule, and some things need to just sit for a while. Ask for help instead of turning healing into a project. For balance, let a little Metal in: declutter, finish old things, clear out the drafts folder. A clean edge helps Wood stop reaching for what's already gone.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means fresh starts feel heavy. After a breakup you might stay in the same place, emotionally and literally, for longer than you'd like. That isn't weakness. It just means new growth needs a nudge. Small steps work best: a new route to work, one new class, one new person a week. Get outside in the mornings and keep something green near you. You don't need a whole new life. You need one new branch, and then another.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire makes you feel everything at full volume. A breakup can feel like an emergency, with urges to text, post, or fix it all tonight. Your passion is real, but heat isn't a strategy. Before any big move, sleep on it. Cool down with water: swimming, long showers, quiet evenings at home. Talk to your calmest friend before your most exciting one. Let the fire warm you instead of burning through your peace.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means joy and visibility don't come easily, and after a breakup you might go dim for a while, hiding from people and from fun. Turn the lights back on gently. Sunshine, music, dancing in the kitchen, one social plan a week even when you'd rather stay in. Letting people see you is the medicine here. Warmth doesn't only live in romance. It's in friends, in laughter, in simply being out in the world.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth means you hold on: to routines, to memories, to the hope that things will settle back into their old place. Stability is your gift, but in heartbreak it can turn into staying stuck. Shake the ground a little. Move the furniture, take a short trip, try something unplanned. Let some Wood energy in, growth and new beginnings. You can keep what was good and still leave room for something new to grow.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth means life can feel unsteady, and a breakup can knock away what little ground you had. You might feel scattered, unsure where to put your feet. Build structure gently: regular meals, a steady bedtime, one place at home that's only yours. Cook something. Walk somewhere. Lean on the people who are reliable. Stability first, big decisions later. You need solid ground under you before deciding anything about the past.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal makes you sharp and decisive, sometimes too quickly. You may have cut the relationship off cleanly and then refused to look at what you feel. Or you judge yourself harshly for every mistake you made in it. Soften the edges. Let Water in: rest, tears, music, journaling. Feeling the grief isn't the same as reopening the door. You can keep your boundaries firm and still let your heart thaw.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are hard, so after a breakup you might keep the door half open, answer every message, or stay friends when it hurts. Practise clean edges. Mute without guilt. Box up their things. Say no without explaining. White and silver, tidy spaces and finished tasks all help your chart. A boundary isn't cold. It's how you protect the part of you that's still healing.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water means you think and feel deeply, maybe endlessly. After a breakup you might drift through memories, analyse every detail, and lose sleep to what-ifs. Your intuition is a gift, but it needs riverbanks. Add some Earth: routines, cooking, walks, people who ground you. Give overthinking a time limit. Feel it fully, then get up and do one ordinary thing.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means rest and reflection get skipped. You may rush past the breakup, staying busy so you never have to sit with it. That works until suddenly it doesn't. Build in quiet on purpose: slow mornings, water by your bed, a few lines in a journal at night, a bath instead of another plan. Let yourself feel without fixing. Intuition grows when you give it some silence.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: So much Wood. You've drafted three versions of 'hey, random but' already.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: That growing energy wants a goal. Give it your own plans, not their inbox.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: every feeling is a five-alarm emergency. It's a breakup, not an inferno.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion is beautiful. Let it cool before you hit send on anything.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Heavy Earth. You'd still be in that relationship purely out of habit.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your loyalty is rare. Just make sure you're loyal to yourself too.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Lots of Metal. You cut them off cleanly, then reread everything at midnight.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Being firm protected you. Being gentle with yourself will heal you.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Overflowing Water: you've cried to three songs and written a novel in your notes app.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Feeling deeply is a gift. Just come up for air sometimes.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood can make moving on feel stuck. Small new routines count as growth.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: You haven't changed anything since the breakup, including your lock screen. Start there.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire can make joy feel far away. Borrow some from a loud friend.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: You stopped having fun when they left. Fun was never theirs to take.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth can make everything feel unsteady. Simple routines will hold you.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: No Earth, no anchor. You re-decide whether to text them every hour.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal makes boundaries tricky. You're allowed to say no to your own phone.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: No Metal means you'll answer at 2am. Put the phone in another room.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water can make grief hide. It's okay to let it surface slowly.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: You said you're fine twelve times today. Water would like a word.

gap-wood.title: The axe and the oak, over the dishwasher
gap-wood.text: You told the truth and they heard a verdict. That's this breakup in one line. Your Gap Wood ex was principled, steady, the kind of person you respect, and you showed that respect the way you always do: by pointing out what could be better. The schedule, the habit, the dishwasher. To you, criticism is care with the decoration removed. To them, it landed like an axe on the trunk, and they defended with speeches about values, which you found preachy, so you pushed harder. Neither of you backed down. Neither of you said sorry first. The texts got efficient and then almost military. And somewhere in there, the warmth you both felt stopped being said. For you the sting is pride: you may still believe you were right about most things, and you might be, and it still ended. The pull is that they could take your bluntness without breaking. Few people can. So practise one soft sentence per day, unrequested. 'You did that well.' 'I like having you around.' It will feel like wearing someone else's jacket. Wear it anyway.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gyeong, I respect the honesty. But 'you're wrong' isn't a love language.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gap, being corrected isn't being rejected. Breathe before the speech.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Two strong people, zero soft sentences. That's the whole post-mortem.

eul-wood.title: The vine wrapped around the blade
eul-wood.text: You fell for a vine, and it wrapped around you in a way nobody else had dared. Your Eul Wood ex softened you. They made you laugh at yourself, which is rare. It was a Heavenly Combination, so you felt the click early. The trouble was the edge. You said things plainly, 'Where are you,' 'That's wrong,' and they took the cut deeper than you ever meant it. They answered with a sticker, a voice note about a cat, a reply that drifted around the question, and you felt managed. You tried to toughen them up, which they heard as 'you're not enough'. When you were hurt, you got sharper. When they were hurt, they slipped away. For you, the sting is feeling like the villain in a story where you were only being honest. What tugs is the gentleness. Nobody else made you feel safe enough to be soft. Add one warm line to every direct one. 'Where are you? Miss you.' It's not weakness. It's a sheath for the blade.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gyeong, 'Where are you.' with a full stop reads like a threat.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Eul, a straight answer first, then the cat. They'd have loved both.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: A great match with a sharp edge. Sheath it, don't break it.

byeong-fire.title: The sun and the blade, forging sparks
byeong-fire.text: You loved someone who needed celebration, and you are not a confetti person. Your Byeong Fire ex sent excitement in capitals with six emojis; you replied 'ok.' and went back to work. To you that was a complete answer. To them, it felt like a door closing. They wanted warmth and fuss; you wanted results and respect. Their heat pressed on you and you resisted being melted, because staying solid is how you feel safe. Your bluntness dimmed them; their bigness made you dig in. The fights were loud and short, and neither of you liked losing. Here is what stings: you did care, a lot, and it never came across. Every 'ok' you sent was an 'I'm here' they couldn't read. What you miss is their light. They made your serious life feel less like a to-do list. Add one warm word to your short replies. 'Ok, can't wait.' 'Done, proud of you.' It isn't softening the metal. It's polishing it so people can see what's inside.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gyeong, 'ok.' with a full stop after their good news? Brutal.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Byeong, short isn't cold. Some people just don't decorate.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Forging takes heat and patience. You had the heat.

jeong-fire.title: The candle and the steel
jeong-fire.text: You said what you meant, and somehow it kept burning the person you loved. Your Jeong Fire ex was thoughtful and warm, and they spoke in subtext. You speak in headlines. You'd say something blunt over breakfast and forget it by lunch; they'd remember it for three weeks. They'd hint at what they needed, and you'd miss it, and then get annoyed that nobody just told you. They tried to soften your edges; you felt like a project. Fights were quiet and deep. You moved on. They didn't. You probably still don't know which sentence did the damage, and that bothers you more than you'd admit. Their patience is what you miss. They kept working on you like slow heat on metal, and part of you was changing. Soften the tone without changing the truth. 'I disagree' instead of 'that's wrong'. 'Can I be honest?' before the honest thing. It's still you. It's just the version people can actually hear, and it keeps your best intentions from arriving as wounds.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gyeong, you forgot the fight by lunch. They're still on it. Know your audience.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Jeong, say the actual thing. Steel can't read candlelight.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Patient heat shapes metal. Silent heat just burns.

mu-earth.title: The mountain holds the ore
mu-earth.text: You were the steel and they were the mountain that held you, and you felt protected without ever saying so. Your Mu Earth ex was steady, proud, unflappable. You were sharp, fast, impatient. You wanted things to change, the plan, the job, the flat, and you wanted it now. They wanted to think about it for a while. A long while. You pushed. They dug in. Your bluntness, which you think of as efficiency, bruised them, and because they don't show hurt, you didn't know. Both of you are proud, so nobody apologised; arguments were brief and heavy, followed by long, stubborn quiet. Looking back, you might feel impatient with yourself. Pushing never once moved them faster. You miss that solidity. With them, you had something to stand on. Practise waiting. Give someone a decision and a deadline twice as long as you'd like. Notice that slow isn't the same as no. Some of the best ore is mined patiently, and some of the best people answer slowly.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gyeong, pushing a mountain is just tiring yourself out.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mu, they couldn't see your bruise. You have to show it.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Strong and stronger. Neither said sorry. Classic.

gi-earth.title: Fertile ground for raw ore
gi-earth.text: You had someone who made everything easier, and you probably didn't realise how much until it stopped. Your Gi Earth ex supported you, quietly and constantly. Dinner was ready. The plans were handled. Your stress was absorbed. You texted 'Done. Coming home.' and they replied 'Great, how did it go?' and you said 'fine' and moved on. Over time, you took that support as the default. You steamrolled their quieter opinions without noticing. Your harsh words landed harder than you knew, because they didn't show the bruise. They held back worries to avoid your impatience, until one day they felt like staff, not a partner, and said so. You weren't trying to be unkind. You just didn't look back. That's the uncomfortable part to own. Their care is the pull. Nobody has made you feel that looked after. Answer the question properly. When someone asks how your day was, tell them, and ask about theirs. It sounds tiny. It's exactly the size of what was missing.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gi, you were a partner, not staff. Say it louder.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gyeong, 'fine' is not an answer to 'how did it go?'

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Patience that shapes strength. Make sure it's thanked.

gyeong-metal.title: Two blades crossed
gyeong-metal.text: Two Gyeong Metals in love: loyal to the death, sharp in the kitchen. 'Where.' 'Here.' 'Ok.' Your texts were efficient to the point of comedy, and honestly, you both liked it. No games, no fluff, no seven-paragraph voice notes. But when you disagreed, neither of you softened a word or backed down an inch, and both of you were convinced you were simply being honest. Small disagreements became battles of will. A debate about the route to the airport could outlast the flight. Neither of you shows vulnerability easily, so hurt came out as anger. Apologies were rare, because apologising felt like losing, and you'd both rather lose a limb. You respected each other more than almost anyone, and it still turned into a duel. That's what's hard to make peace with. The loyalty is what pulls you. You knew they'd fight for you, and that's rare. Practise the one move neither of you made. Say 'I was wrong' first, out loud, about something small. Then add a silly emoji to a serious text, just to see what disarming feels like. Neither will make you weaker. Both are sharper than any blade.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: 'Where.' 'Here.' 'Ok.' Romantic, in a military way.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You both fought so hard. Imagine fighting for each other instead.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Say 'I was wrong' first. It won't kill you. Probably.

sin-metal.title: Steel and silver
sin-metal.text: Same metal, different polish. You're the raw steel; your Sin Metal ex was the silver. You spoke bluntly; they found it crude. They spoke precisely, with layers; you found it nitpicky. You'd say something careless at dinner, scratch their polish, and not notice. They'd cut you with one quiet, sarcastic sentence on the way home, and you'd notice a lot. Pride ran high on both sides. Neither apologised first. A typical fight started with something you said without thinking and ended with something they said very much on purpose. You felt judged for being straightforward, and you never could decode what they actually wanted. That combination wore you down. The respect is what pulls. They had standards, and you liked meeting them. Soften the delivery. Same truth, gentler packaging. 'I think there's a better way' instead of 'that's wrong'. And when someone says something layered, ask: 'What do you actually mean?' Subtext isn't your language. Asking is, and there's no shame in a blade that asks before it cuts.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Sin, they missed your subtext. Every single time. Stop sending it.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gyeong, soften the delivery. Keep the honesty.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Same metal. Different polish. Equal pride.

im-water.title: Cold steel, deep water
im-water.text: Cold steel, deep water. Metal feeds water, and you did: you gave your Im Water ex structure, clarity, a solid edge to push against. They gave you depth and big ideas. Both of you are clear thinkers, and the conversations were brilliant, the kind that go until the bar closes. But you wanted commitment and clear plans, and they wanted freedom and flexibility. Your bluntness could chill them. Their unpredictability frustrated you. Both of you are independent, so emotional closeness lagged behind practical partnership. You were excellent teammates and not quite lovers. It worked on paper, and you still can't fully explain why it didn't work in the heart. That's the itch you keep scratching. Their mind is what you miss. You respected it more than almost anyone's. Practise being close, not just useful. Share something you're unsure about. Ask for help with something small. Let someone see you mid-thought instead of finished. Closeness grows from the soft places, and you have more of them than you show.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Great minds. Great teammates. Remember to be lovers too.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gyeong, a calendar invite is not a love letter.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Im, freedom with a check-in is still freedom.

gye-water.title: The sword and the morning dew
gye-water.text: Tough love with a soft centre. Your Gye Water ex was gentle, intuitive, mysterious, and you felt protective of them from the start. But your bluntness could hurt them deeply. You sent one-line orders of the day; they sent a photo of the fog with no caption, and you had no idea what it meant. When you wanted answers right now, they needed a day to know what they felt. The worst nights were the ones where you pushed for a straight answer at midnight and got a long, sad silence instead, and both of you went to sleep misunderstood. You became overprotective, sometimes controlling; they withdrew, sometimes keeping things to themselves. You were trying to keep them safe, and they felt kept. The softness is what pulls you. They saw the tender part of you most people never get near. Ask what the photo means. Ask what they feel, then wait, actually wait, for the answer. Gentleness won't make you less of a sword. It makes you a sword people trust.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gye, a captionless fog photo is not an answer to 'dinner at 8?'

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gyeong, ask what the photo means. Then wait.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Tough love needs a soft centre. You had one. Use it.
